content:
Renee Sullivan: hey DevEx folks — looking for a quick gut-check on the demo scripts + quickstart draft. what’s confusing / too many steps / unsafe defaults? want this to be “SE can run it live w/ 0 surprises”. link to draft: https://drive.google.com/redwood/demo/Sales-Demo-Quickstart (also PRs in flight: redwood-quickstarts#613, redwood-examples#842)

Elliot Price: skimmed. biggest thing: we’re asking people to copy/paste 6 curl commands before anything interesting happens. can we collapse to 1-2 “happy path” commands?

Elliot Price: suggestion: add a tiny wrapper CLI (or at least a `Makefile`) so the README becomes:
- `cp .env.example .env`
- `source .env`
- `make demo-chat-stream`
- `make demo-fallback`
then keep the raw curl in an “under the hood” section.

Colin O'Donnell: +1. the talk track wants “type one command and see streaming tokens”. right now first command is `models list` and then you pick ids — feels like we’re front-loading the catalog.

Simran Kaur: agree. also the current examples hardcode `temperature=0.8` in one place and `0.2` elsewhere. for live demo we should default to low variance.

Simran Kaur: maybe set defaults:
- `temperature=0.2`
- `top_p=1`
- `max_tokens=220` (cap cost + latency)
- and if we need creativity, call it out as an explicit “turn it up” step.

Amara Diallo: from API gateway POV: please set an explicit request timeout in the examples. we keep seeing folks run curl and then it “hangs” because network/streaming. add `--max-time 60` on non-streaming and for streaming show `--no-buffer` + a note.

Elliot Price: + docs nit: we mix “Hosted endpoint” and “Dedicated endpoint” terminology without defining the base URL patterns. could we add a one-liner banner:
- Hosted: `https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/...`
- Dedicated: `https://<tenant>.dedicated.redwoodinference.com/v1/...`
- Private: “depends; see your deployment”

Colin O'Donnell: the other confusing part is auth. we show `Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY` but then later we introduce `REDWOOD_DEMO_TOKEN`. pick one env var and stick to it.

Renee Sullivan: makes sense. we used `REDWOOD_DEMO_TOKEN` because the demo tenant key is scoped/rotated, but we can alias it.

Cole Summers: jumping in re: safer defaults (quotas/rate limits). the sample calls use `concurrency=8` in the batching example. pls don’t do that by default for demo tenant. it increases odds of 429s if someone runs it right before a live demo.

Cole Summers: recommend:
- default concurrency 1
- add a “load test” section that’s explicitly labeled NOT FOR LIVE DEMO
- and for any script that loops, add `sleep 0.2` to avoid burst throttles.

Nikhil Sharma: +1. also: the “cost controls” demo currently tells user to toggle batching + caching and then rerun a long prompt. can we ship a short prompt that still shows cost delta? (like 150-250 tokens) so it’s quick.

Simran Kaur: yes — we can use a prompt with repeated prefix to make caching obvious without being huge. e.g. “You are an assistant that extracts fields…” + a few sample inputs.

Elliot Price: + we should add a “demo mode” warning banner at top:
- don’t paste customer data
- everything typed may be logged in demo tenant (even if sanitized)
- use provided canned prompts

Elliot Price: also please avoid printing env vars in scripts. one of the bash snippets does `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY` as a debug tip. remove.

Amara Diallo: :100: on not echoing secrets. also minor: ensure all requests include `X-Request-Id` in examples. it helps when someone pings #support “it failed” and we have nothing.

Colin O'Donnell: good call. we can generate one inline: `RID=$(uuidgen)` and pass it.

Talia Benson: capturing actions (tell me if I missed):
1) Add `Makefile` targets for the 4 main scenarios (chat streaming, structured output, tool calling, fallback routing)
2) Push raw curl down into “reference” section
3) Standardize env vars + endpoints section
4) Safer defaults: low temp, small max tokens, concurrency=1
5) Add timeouts + request id headers

Renee Sullivan: looks right.

Colin O'Donnell: one more: the python snippet uses `asyncio` and it’s a lot for people. can we provide a dead-simple sync snippet first?

Elliot Price: yes pls. “pip install redwood-sdk” + 10 lines, then optional async/advanced.

Simran Kaur: also: in tool calling example, the “tool” returns current time. that’s nondeterministic + can derail expected output comparisons. use a deterministic tool like `lookup_shipping_zone(zip)` with a tiny static map.

Nikhil Sharma: :+1: deterministic. otherwise we’ll get “why did it say 3:02pm” in a recording.

Cole Summers: and ensure examples set `seed` if we support it (or at least call out “outputs vary” once, early). otherwise AEs will panic.

Amara Diallo: seed is supported on the demo models we pinned, right?

Colin O'Donnell: for the two main demo models, yes. (we pinned versions specifically for this.) we’ll add `seed: 42` in the JSON body for the known-good scenarios.

Renee Sullivan: awesome. I’ll update the draft + PR with:
- Makefile
- sync python snippet
- deterministic tool example
- safe defaults + timeouts
and loop back for another quick review.

Elliot Price: ping me on the PR. happy to review wording + structure.

Talia Benson: I’ll add these to the checklist + make sure they line up with the talk track.

Renee Sullivan: thx all :thumbsup: (also if anyone has a strong opinion on naming: `make demo-chat` vs `make demo_streaming_chat`, reply here)

Elliot Price: `make demo-chat` is fine. keep targets short. (we can print what it’s doing.)

Colin O'Donnell: +1 short. just make sure `make help` lists targets + one-line descriptions.

Renee Sullivan: done. closing loop after updates.
